title: French citizens prepare for fourth consecutive Saturday of cost of living protests

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, low purchasing power, and economic policies.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand government action on purchasing power, wages, and support for young people.
tea.changed: Nov 7: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez deployed 70,000 security personnel nationwide as Yellow Vests defied a ban in central Paris.

summary: French unions, student groups, and Yellow Vests activists are organising demonstrations across the country and in Paris for another consecutive Saturday of cost-of-living protests. The movement follows weeks of nationwide strikes, youth-led unrest, and prior large-scale demonstrations over inflation and purchasing power. While trade unions and student organisations scheduled authorised marches, Yellow Vests called for a separate rally at Place de la Concorde in central Paris despite an official ban by local authorities. In response, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced the deployment of 70,000 police officers and gendarmes across France, alongside armoured vehicles, water cannons, and drones. Authorities banned protests in several city centres following earlier clashes and property damage during previous mobilizations.
demands: Measures to address the high cost of living
Action on wages and purchasing power
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez deployed 70,000 police officers and security forces nationwide, utilising armoured vehicles, water cannons, and drones, while city center bans were enforced by prefects.

updates.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced 70,000 police and gendarmes would be mobilised for Saturday's demonstrations.
Yellow Vests planned a banned rally in central Paris while unions and student groups organised authorised marches.
